notes.summary: Raw geometric envelope calculus, exact primary-gauge changes, and actual decreasing-net closure are reconstructed without assuming universal envelope continuity.
notes.detailedSummary: Relative to entire qualified G331, the raw C and D envelopes agree for finite continuous obstacles, are nonexpansive, and have an intrinsic factorial-primary-ideal formula. Continuity, geometric positivity, and existence of a greatest or maximal D minorant are equivalent. Decreasing-D closure is proved by insertion, rather than by flattening nested nets. Continuous-envelope sectors consequently have greatest extended-USC envelopes represented by one decreasing C-net.
notes.text:
Use the entire qualified G331, including its actual-primary-model, source, all-support, smooth-specialization and conductor qualifications. Let X={v:v(a)=1}, C be the continuous geometric uniform cone, and D its actual decreasing-C-net completion. No envelope theorem is imported.

For finite continuous f, define p(f)=sup{h in D:h<=f}. A sufficiently negative primary constant is a competitor. If h_i decreases to h<=f, the open sets {h_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X. Directedness gives one index valid everywhere. Then h_i-epsilon is a C competitor below f and above h-epsilon. Thus the raw C and D suprema agree. Their value is finite, bounded and lower semicontinuous. Negative shifts prove ||p(f)-p(g)||<=||f-g||; unrestricted positive constant translation is unnecessary.

If p(f) is continuous, finitely many continuous competitors and their maximum approximate it uniformly from below, so p(f) belongs to C. Membership in D implies upper semicontinuity, hence continuity. A greatest minorant is exactly p(f). A maximal minorant is greatest because D is closed under finite maxima. If p(f)* belongs to D, continuity of f gives p(f)*<=f; it is a competitor and therefore equals p(f). These are equivalent positivity and regularity conditions, not an automatic consequence of upper regularization.

Set J_k(f)={r:v(r)>=-k f(v) for all v in X}. These are unit-or-primary ideals containing a primary power, are integrally closed by the monic least-term test after quotienting by the valuation support, and satisfy J_k J_l subset J_(k+l). Rational-profile density and negative shifts give p(f)=sup_k[-v(J_k)/k]=sup_n[-v(J_(n!))/n!]. The factorial profiles increase. This formula supplies no increasing-D closure.

Actual decreasing-D closure is obtained by insertion. On a normal branch, the G331 zero dichotomy leaves either the all-zero case or a tail bounded above by -c<0. For u_i decreasing to u and finite continuous F>u, compact strict tests select u_i<F and then a continuous representation term g with u_i<=g<F and g<-c/2. A sufficiently small b>0 makes (1-b)g strictly between u and F. Apply insertion to the minimum of two continuous majorants. They are downward directed. Urysohn cutoffs show their infimum equals u pointwise, including bottom. They form ONE actual decreasing C-net. For reduced germs apply this on the finitely many normal centres and use full-fibre G331 D descent.

If CE denotes continuity of every finite continuous raw envelope, all finite continuous nonpositive majorants of a bounded-above extended USC obstacle form a minimum-directed family with the obstacle as infimum. Their envelopes are ONE decreasing C-net; its limit is the greatest D minorant. Decreasing-obstacle-net stability follows using the preceding actual closure theorem, with specified USC limits.

For another primary gauge b, put d(v)=v(b), T(v)=v/d(v). The bounded positive denominator and its inverse preserve uniform and decreasing representations. Transform both obstacle and potential by u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). Order and the raw supremum give the exact envelope cocycle p_b(f_b)(Tv)=p_a(f_a)(v)/d(v).

Complete proofs are in whole-proof.md Section1 and P12.3-independent-paper.tex. These are unverified mathematical arguments relative to the qualified grant, not consequences of execution.

notes.summary: ROOT380 passes at its exact embedding hypotheses; the distinct ample globally generated Koszul theorem also passes. Trace applications remain conditional.
notes.detailedSummary: The affine-base regularity proof works over finite-type algebras over any field, including finite fields, without coherent-sheaf base flatness. Its very ample version requires vanishings through the projective embedding dimension N. The separate Koszul proof uses an ample globally generated bundle and coherent cohomological dimension dim Y. Both give generation of fixed finite lists of Frobenius sheaves, but neither proves a trace presentation.
notes.text:
Independent verdict: PASS for the entire ROOT380 lemma with its precise hypotheses and conditional application scope.

Let R be finite type over any field k, G coherent on P^N_R, and H^i(G(-i))=0 for 1<=i<=N. Pass faithfully flatly to an infinite field only to choose a constant hyperplane. A finite affine Cech complex proves flat cohomology base change, and the evaluation cokernel proves generation descent. No flatness of G over R is assumed.

The finitely many associated points give finitely many proper linear conditions on constant hyperplane coefficients: some projective coordinate is nonzero at each point. Avoid their union over the infinite field. Multiplication by the chosen equation is injective, giving 0->G(-1)->G->G'->0 with G' on P^(N-1)_R. Its long exact sequence proves zero-regularity of G'. Induct simultaneously on dimension and twist. The same sequence propagates H^i(G(t-i))=0 to every t>=0; groups beyond N vanish by projective cohomological dimension. Restrict a section of G(t+1) to the hyperplane, use multiplication surjectivity there, lift the coefficient sections using H^1(G(t-1))=0, and express the remaining section as the hyperplane equation times a section of G(t). This proves multiplication surjectivity. High Serre generation and repeated multiplication then prove generation of G itself. Descend by faithful flatness. For an embedded Y use its coherent direct image. Very ampleness and conditions through N are binding.

The different 382 Koszul proof also works. Let A be ample globally generated on finite-dimensional projective Y over a noetherian affine base, and suppose H^i(M A^(-i))=0 for 1<=i<=dim Y. Finitely many generating sections have a locally split exact Koszul complex; tensoring with M preserves exactness. Its terms propagate Reg(t) to Reg(t+1), using the groups in successively higher degrees and the cohomological dimension bound. The same full complex gives multiplication surjectivity in nonnegative twists. High Serre generation concludes. The full complex, rather than just its first short sequence, is essential. No smoothness, CM or sheaf base-flatness is used.

For fixed Cartier L and H with A=O(H), choose c0 such that (c0-i)H-L is ample for every required i. For a fixed finite coherent list M_j, projection formula reduces regularity of F_*^e(M_j O(p^e(c0H-L))) to Serre vanishing. Frobenius is finite on finite-type schemes over perfect fields. The Serre threshold may depend on the list; c0 does not. The very ample argument uses i<=N, while the Koszul argument uses i<=dim Y.

Generation of a trace target follows only if it has exact arbitrarily late tail presentations and a finite quotient from possibly DIFFERENT exponents and finitely many residues. ROOT380 does not prove those presentations, a global test divisor, singular subadditivity or envelope positivity.

Complete current Stacks01YS,02OI,0B5U and0B5T immediate statements/proofs were inspected, with the partial0B5U response superseded by its complete retained unit. Their recursive coherent-cohomology foundations are disclosed ordinary background. Complete independent arguments are in whole-proof.md Section2.

notes.summary: ROOT381 passes. HH02 supplies generators with potentially different normalizations; generatorwise lifting repairs 382 without imperfect-field Frobenius descent.
notes.detailedSummary: The perfect-extension Frobenius/Hom/diagonal kernel-and-image theorem holds for any finite-type algebra, without reducedness or normality. The Jacobian application separately requires the infinite-perfect reduced-equidimensional inclusion. HH02 Theorem3.4 does not provide one normalization for each arbitrary Jacobian element, and K(t) is not generally perfect. The repair runs its generic-coordinate proof directly over an infinite perfect field, uses finite free polynomial root modules, adds generatorwise lifts, and descends through a perfect extension. Historical HH/LS/Kunz foundations are expressly not claimed freshly verified.
notes.text:
Independent ROOT381 verdict: PASS for its entire module theorem, with the application gate retained.

For perfect k subset k' and q=p^e, the explicit R'=R tensor_k k' identification is Phi(F_*x tensor c)=F_*(x tensor c^q). Its inverse uses c^(1/q). The balance relation and Frobenius scalar action prove linearity. Bounded-exponent monomials give finite Frobenius modules for every finite-type algebra, including nonreduced ones. No normality premise is needed.

For S=R tensor_k R and I=ker(S->R), compatible maps form the kernel of Hom_S(F_*S,S)->Hom_S(F_*I,R). Finite presentations express Hom as matrix kernels. Flat extension preserves those kernels, the compatibility kernel, and the image of quotient restriction into Hom_R(F_*R,R). The cokernel gives faithful descent of image membership. Differentials and fixed-index Fitting ideals commute with extension by their finite presentations and minors. This proves diagonal liftability descent, not test-ideal field base change or subadditivity by itself.

Literal382 has a precise HH02 defect. Complete Theorem3.4 says that after K(t), Jac is GENERATED by elements c, EACH with a potentially DIFFERENT generically etale polynomial normalization A satisfying c R^(1/q) subset A^(1/q)[R], with A^(1/q)[R] identified with A^(1/q) tensor_A R. It does not say every arbitrary Jac element has one such normalization. K(t) need not be perfect, so the preceding Phi cannot be applied blindly there.

The immediate HH02 generic-coordinate proof can instead be run directly over an already infinite PERFECT field. Its finite generic open coordinate conditions have rational points. Each complementary Jacobian minor has its corresponding generically etale polynomial normalization; the cited Lipman--Sathaye root containment applies generatorwise. Over the perfect field, A^(1/q) is finite FREE over A, with the coordinate monomial basis of exponents below q.

Here is the lifting construction. Write T=R^(1/q), P=A^(1/q)[R], B=R tensor_k T. P tensor_k T is free over B. Multiplication B->T is onto, so the B-linear multiplication P tensor T->T lifts to Psi:P tensor T->B. For phi:T->R, compose T tensor T --(c tensor 1)--> P tensor T --Psi--> R tensor T --(1 tensor phi)--> R tensor R. After diagonal multiplication its value on x tensor y is phi(cxy)=c phi(xy). It therefore vanishes on the diagonal root kernel and induces c phi. In F_* notation the required precomposition is multiplication by c^q inside the source. The quotient-restriction image is an R-module, so summing the lifts with coefficients proves Jac times Hom subset the diagonal restriction image. One normalization for an arbitrary sum is unnecessary.

For a finite perfect field, extend to an infinite PERFECT field, such as the perfection of k(t), apply that generatorwise inclusion, and descend by the proved kernel/image and fixed-Fitting theorem. The normal finite-type application is geometrically reduced and equidimensional. These are separate application hypotheses; they are not required for ROOT381's module lemma. The printed use of a k-linear retraction as an extension-field action is invalid and is not used.

Smolkin's complete Sections2/3 then give the BIG corrected subadditivity formula Jac tau(ab) subset tau(a)tau(b): full-map tensoring and quotient restriction yield tau_D(ab) subset tau(a)tau(b), while generatorwise Jac inclusion with a common big test element gives Jac tau(ab) subset tau_D(ab). Common-multiple asymptotic stabilization and iteration give Jac^(l-1) s_(ml) subset s_m^l, in this direction.

The complete immediately applied HH02 statement/proof and preceding3.2/3.3 context were read. Its recursive inputs HH6(1.5.5), Lipman--Sathaye/reduced-equidimensional variant, HH2Lemma6.4 and Kunz are disclosed published foundations; their historical proofs were NOT all freshly authenticated. Scoped acceptance uses the permitted ordinary published-background rule, not a claim of a newly verified historical proof tree. Complete argument: whole-proof.md Section3.

notes.summary: The repaired isolated closed normal perfect-charp theorem has all-support continuous geometric envelopes, including non-CM canonical flattening and actual-primary uniform recognition.
notes.detailedSummary: For an isolated normal closed finite-type germ over any perfect positive-characteristic field, dimension at least two, every finite primary collection and gauge admits the required canonical-flattened actual primary model. Scheme-global big trace generation uses fixed c0, possibly varying test divisors and arbitrarily late multi-exponent tails. Actual primary profiles converge uniformly with error (c+a+b)N_J/m on every support. This proves the scoped theorem; it does not cover arbitrary nonisolated, imperfect, mixed or nonalgebraic germs.
notes.text:
Use n1--n3 and entire qualified G331. Let B be normal integral affine finite type over a perfect positive-characteristic field, x CLOSED of codimension at least two, with regular puncture after shrinking. Include the gauge in any finite collection of primary ideals.

Blow up their product and normalize. Every factor is invertible: an invertible product of nonzero ideals gives a fractional inverse, and a unit product in a local expression of 1 makes each factor principal with regular generator. The product gives a full-fibre Cartier F0 with negative ample bundle. On the normal model the canonical module is coherent torsion-free rank one even if the scheme is non-CM. Blow up Fitt1(omega). On each actual chart R[G/a] subset R_a, its strict transform has Fitt1 unit and Fitt0 zero, the latter because it vanishes after inverting a in a domain. The Fitting criterion makes it invertible. Normalize and pull back this line bundle.

Use the SAME rational section for its Cartier divisor L0 and K_Y. Their difference is exceptional as a divisor. Choose r with Delta=rF0-(K_Y-L0)>=0; then L=K_Y+Delta=L0+rF0 is Cartier. The negative Fitting boundary times a high pullback power of O(-F0), followed by finite normalization and a high power, gives a full-fibre very ample globally generated A=O(-F). Hartogs puts J=Gamma(Y,A) in B. It is proper primary, and J O_Y=A. A generating very ample immersion has exactly the punctured graph defining J. Integrality and identical scheme-theoretic graph closure prove Y=Bl_J B, not merely domination of an arbitrary model.

Fix J^a O_Y subset Jac(Y/k), Delta<=bF and a_gauge^(N_J) subset J. Perfectness makes the regular puncture smooth, so Jac is unit there. These inclusions give v(Jac)<=a v(J)<=aN_J on EVERY support.

For an integral exceptional Cartier obstacle C0, evaluation first uses Frac(B/support(v)) and the proper centre of its valuation ring. The punctured trivialization gives a nonzero local generator. No map from Frac(B) through a nonzero support is used. Let I_m=Gamma(Y,O(mC0)) and b_m=I_m O_Y O(-mC0). Hartogs gives an actual unit-or-primary ideal I_m for EVERY m; an actual Cartier order bound supplies a_gauge^(Mm) subset I_m. Products give gradedness. Thus u_m=-v(I_m)/m=f_C0-v(b_m)/m<=f_C0. All-index Fekete, including finite remainder values, gives lim_m u_m=sup_m u_m without asserting monotonicity.

EVERY rational profile -v(I)/q below f_C0 satisfies I^r subset I_(rq): test every exceptional height-one point of the NORMAL model, use regularity off the fibre, then normal height-one intersection. Rational density, negative shifts and n1's C/D argument prove raw p(f_C0)=lim u_m on all supports BEFORE positivity recognition.

Use CEMS v4 BIG test ideals. Power invariance follows from ceil(qt)<=r ceil(qt/r)<=ceil(qt)+r-1 and multiplication of a common big test element by a nonzero element of b^r. Gradedness gives common-multiple directedness and noetherian stabilization. Put t_m=tau(Y,Delta,b_bullet^m), s_m=tau(Y,b_bullet^m). Choose c0 ONCE with (c0-i)H-L ample for every required i, H=-F. For fixed m choose ell attaining t_m.

A GLOBAL Cartier test divisor exists: dominate affine test-element zeros and finite rounding corrections by effective Weil E; generated O(-E)A^r has a nonzero section defining Cartier D0>=E. Normal height-one regularity makes its local equations multiples of all local test elements. The arbitrary-late-tail trace formula therefore glues with one D0. D0 and ell may depend on m; c0 cannot.

Set q=p^e, a_e=ceil(qm/ell), j_e=ell a_e-qm in 0..ell-1. Global section products from I_ell generate b_ell^(a_e)O(ell a_e C0). After twisting the target by O(mC0+c0H), the sources are quotients of copies of Q_(e,j)=F_*O(q(c0H-L)+K_Y-D0-jC0). Multiplication by section products occurs INSIDE F_* and is linear for the Frobenius scalar action. The finitely many reflexive factors O(K_Y-D0-jC0) are fixed for this m. n2 and Serre vanishing generate every sufficiently late Q_(e,j). The arbitrary tail may stabilize as a finite sum using DIFFERENT exponents; a single exponent is not assumed. Hence t_m O(mC0+c0H) is generated.

Take c=c0+1. The section ideal J_m of t_m O(mC0)A^c is actual primary. Before the extra A twist, generation by sections in B makes the sheaf a subsheaf of O_Y; the extra twist makes it contained in J O_Y. T0=tau(Y,Delta) is unit off the fibre and contains J^r O_Y. The common-test-element identity b_m T0 subset t_m gives I_m J^(r+c) subset J_m. Thus g_m=-v(J_m)/m=f_C0-(c v(J)+v(t_m))/m is an actual C competitor.

Now b_(ml)T0 subset t_(ml) subset s_(ml) and the correctly directed n3 inclusion Jac^(l-1)s_(ml) subset s_m^l give
v(s_m)/m <= [v(b_(ml))+v(T0)]/(ml)+(l-1)v(Jac)/(ml).
All values are finite because the ideals contain primary powers. FIRST let l tend to infinity at the fixed valuation. With h=f_C0-p(f_C0), Fekete gives v(s_m)<=m h+v(Jac). The Cartier shift and Delta<=bF give O(-bF)s_m subset t_m subset s_m. Therefore
0<=p(f_C0)-g_m <=[(c+b)v(J)+v(Jac)]/m <=(c+a+b)N_J/m.
The last error is uniform on ALL supports. Uniform limits of actual primary profiles recognize p(f_C0) in C.

Signed-primary lattice density carries every finite continuous obstacle through a finite primary collection on the constructed model. Nonexpansivity completes CE. n1 supplies ONE-net extended-USC envelopes, decreasing-obstacle stability and the exact gauge cocycle.

Independent scoped verdict: PASS for this repaired theorem, as an unverified mathematical draft with n3's explicit recursive published-foundation qualification. No smooth resolution, anticanonical finite generation, increasing-D closure or nonprimary correction bound is assumed. Full proof: whole-proof.md Sections4--6.

notes.summary: The surrounding surface, isolated char0 and exact BFJ smooth chain passes at its precise hypotheses; the nonisolated char0 infinite-Q locus remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Excellent normal surfaces have CE in every characteristic and residue field via actual regular primary models, the exceptional matrix and its greatest feasible vector. Closed isolated normal algebraic germs over algebraically closed characteristic zero have CE using correctly directed upper coefficient approximations and finite-trace uniformity. Smooth BFJ specialization retains its published all-support and closed-face scope. General char0 correction estimates give only local uniformity on the finite-Q locus.
notes.text:
The surrounding arguments are reconstructed independently, not imported from older376/377 labels.

For an excellent normal local surface, normalize a product-primary blowup and apply the current dimension-two resolution criterion. Finite singular locus, finite normalization and normal completions hold at the stated excellent normal models. The projective regular surface is unchanged off the closed point. Stein factorization gives Gamma O=R and connected fibre. This is a dimension-TWO application only.

Write F_a=sum b_iE_i with every b_i>0, and M=(E_iE_j). Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative; the graph is connected; M b<=0 with a strict entry from the gauge blowup's tautological ampleness. For A=-M and t_i=b_i z_i,
t^t A t=sum_i(Ab)_i b_i z_i^2+sum_(i<j)(-A_ij)b_i b_j(z_i-z_j)^2.
Thus A is positive definite. Pairing a hypothetical negative part with A proves every principal inverse is nonnegative. Consequently A^(-1)1 is strictly positive rational. Clearing denominators yields an effective full-fibre Cartier divisor whose negative bundle has positive degree on every fibre curve. The ample criterion applies to the FULL possibly nonreduced fibre over any residue field. Fibre ampleness, high generation and the identical punctured graph give an ACTUAL regular primary blowup carrying the specified ideals.

On a common regular refinement, push a negative curve-nef Cartier D' to D. Actual cycle projection gives D.E>=0. For F=D'-mu*D, the contracted principal matrix satisfies M_J f>=0, hence f<=0. Therefore D'<=mu*D at all supports. This trace inequality passes through uniform C limits and bounded actual D representations. For a signed obstacle the feasible coefficient polytope is -B b_i<=z_i<=min(0,c_i), Mz>=0. It is nonempty, compact and stable under coordinate maximum. Maxima of coordinate maximizers give its greatest vector. Its negative curve-nef Cartier evaluation dominates EVERY D competitor, using one continuous term at the finitely many trace tests and a negative shift. It is the raw envelope. Signed lattice density proves CE for every excellent normal surface, including mixed characteristic and imperfect residue fields.

For characteristic zero the THREE-author BdFF source is applied only to normal algebraic germs over an ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED characteristic-zero field. Its largest-trace envelope W is below the signed determining Cartier obstacle, has base trace zero and is nonpositive. At a CLOSED isolated singularity, source4.11 gives primary/unit Cartier UPPER approximations B_k>=W, coefficientwise. Denominators are cleared first. Their finitely many determining-vertex excesses eta_k tend to zero. Largest-trace maximality gives B_k+eta_k Z(a)<=W<=B_k on every divisorial valuation. The continuous primary profiles are uniformly Cauchy on the divisorially dense full link. Their limit U belongs to C. Selecting ONE continuous representation term at the determining trace tests controls every D competitor by U. Thus U is the raw envelope. Zero/unit and eventual proper-primary exceptions are retained.

In general nonisolated characteristic zero the correction Q=d(K)Jac may be nonprimary. Primary truncation gives estimates W-v(Q)/(Nk)<=u_k<=W+eta_k. Extend continuous differences FIRST on the OPEN finite-Q locus using divisorial density, then restrict to {v(Q)<=L}; density on that closed subset is not presumed. Shifted competitors converge locally uniformly there to the raw envelope. The infinite-Q support stratum is not resolved. Unbounded correction values are not counterexamples.

At a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, G331 gives exact BFJ class specialization. The complete BFJ3.18/3.22 argument gives W_j<=W<=j W_j/(j+C0), with primary-reference bounded uniform error. Substantive closed-face continuity and ALL-retraction infima extend this to every support. Unit/zero, eventual proper-primary, bottom, DVR and empty cases are treated separately. Thus the constructed envelope equals the published smooth BFJ envelope within that precise scope.

GJKM4.6 is used only on an ACTUAL smooth integral primary model projective over an AFFINE finite-type perfect-field base. Its fixed canonical twist and smooth subadditivity yield error c v(J)/m. The corrected Keeler v5 proof and ENTIRE erratum repair its cited vanishing step. Existence of such smooth primary models for every finite collection remains a gate; GJKM4.6 is not applied to singular models.

Complete proofs and immediate-source restrictions are in whole-proof.md Section7 and source-ledger.md. Source historical resolution, multiplier, numerical-b-divisor and cohomology foundations are disclosed ordinary published dependencies, not a newly verified recursive proof tree.

notes.summary: Actual finite dominating-cover transfer proves CE for the nonisolated quadratic family in every perfect charp, including nonflat purely inseparable characteristic two.
notes.detailedSummary: A normal target inherits CE from an actual finite reduced cover whose every minimal component dominates and whose marked centres have CE. Full finite-fibre maxima preserve C and D by the qualified normal trace and positive descent. Quadratic cone times affine space has such a finite smooth cover of generic degree two in every perfect characteristic; its closed fibre has length three, including the radicial characteristic-two case.
notes.text:
Let normal R inject finitely into reduced S, with EVERY minimal source component dominating R. Qualified G331's normal coefficient trace has positive full finite-fibre support, including generic inseparable lengths and quotient-support valuations. Normalize the generic components in a common field closure and take the finite conjugate maximum of a C function. It stays in C, is full-fibre constant and descends positively. Thus fibrewise maximum preserves C. Finite maxima commute with decreasing nonpositive extended nets by finite directedness, so the same holds for D.

For a base obstacle f, a source competitor below rho*f has its fibre maximum descend to a base competitor. Conversely base competitors pull back. Therefore p_S(rho*f)=rho*p_R(f). If every marked source centre has CE, the left side is continuous C. Compact quotient topology and full-fibre positive descent imply target CE. Vertical minimal components are excluded rather than assigned invented generic degrees. A proper alteration with positive-dimensional fibres is not this finite cover.

Take R=k[U,V,W,z]/(UW-V^2) localized at the origin, and S=k[s,t,z] localized there, with U=s^2,V=st,W=t^2. R is integral, CM and regular in codimension one, so normal. The map is finite since s,t are integral. Its generic degree is two, separable outside characteristic two and radicial in characteristic two. The closed fibre has basis 1,s,t and length three, so the map is nonflat of generic rank two.

Nevertheless S is an ACTUAL finite smooth cover in every perfect positive characteristic. n4 applies to its regular closed source, and the finite-cover theorem proves CE for every number of z variables. With at least one z variable the target is nonisolated. In algebraically closed characteristic zero use n5's BFJ source CE instead. Thus the nonprimary Jacobian correction failure on this family is not a counterexample, including the nonflat purely inseparable characteristic-two case.

Complete argument: whole-proof.md Section8. No universal good-cover hypothesis, arbitrary finite-map operator theorem or alteration-to-cover replacement is asserted.

notes.summary: The full finite-continuous conductor positivity criterion and genuine nonnormal obstruction are proved; every reduced curve has geometric clipping. Energy diagnostics do not recognize increasing-limit positivity.
notes.detailedSummary: Under normal-centre CE, downstairs regularization is the full-fibre maximum of upstairs envelopes, and geometric positivity occurs exactly when those envelopes are full-fibre constant. Extended-USC obstacles retain a constrained competitor identity, not an ungated maximum formula. The double plane has a continuous negative obstacle with no maximal D minorant. Curves have actual Cartier/DVR positivity and clipping for all branch patterns. The existing smooth and quadratic energy spikes are diagnostic increasing limits, not normal raw-envelope counterexamples.
notes.text:
Let S normalize an excellent reduced germ, rho its full compact link quotient and c its conductor. G331 supplies singleton fibres at finite conductor value and exact conductor-quotient identifications at infinite value, retaining internal and nonpure supports. The finite-value singleton locus is open and dense upstairs because c contains a regular element and divisorial points are dense on every normal centre.

For finite continuous f clipped to [-B,0], clamp a source competitor g below by -B. The PRIMARY masks b_N=-(B/N)v(c+a^N) are C functions, equal -B on the infinite-conductor locus and tending to zero at every finite-conductor point. The function max(g+rho*b_N,-B) is full-fibre constant and descends POSITIVELY by G331. Consequently rho*p_R(f)=p_S(rho*f) on the finite-conductor locus. No uniform nonprimary conductor error is used.

If every normal centre has CE, let U=p_S(rho*f) in C_S. Dense equality gives the upstairs regularization U. For a compact quotient, covering the whole fibre and removing the closed image of the complement proves F*(x)=max_(rho^-1 x)(rho*F)*. Therefore p_R(f)*(x)=max_fibre U. This is a regularization identity, not automatic positivity.

Positive greatest minorants occur exactly when U is constant on EVERY full fibre. In that case its positive C descent is below f and equals the raw envelope. Conversely continuity of the raw envelope forces its pullback to equal U by dense agreement. Continuity of the fibre maximum similarly forces compatibility. By n1 these are also equivalent to maximal-D-minorant existence. Outside that domain no maximal minorant exists. Without normal-centre CE, the exact positive criterion is continuity and full-fibre constancy of the upstairs raw envelope itself. Extended-USC/pole obstacles retain only the supremum over full-fibre-constant source D competitors; the finite-continuous maximum formula is not extended without proof.

A genuine NONNORMAL obstruction occurs on R=k[x,y,z]/(xy) at the origin. On the two normal planes A=k[x,z], B=k[y,z], take the continuous obstacle f=-1-1/v(y), with 1/infinity=0. It is -1 on A and lies in [-2,-1]. On B every normalized primary profile, hence every C,D function, satisfies g(v)<=g(ord_m); any competitor is therefore at most -2.

On A use J_n=(x^n,xz^(n-1),z^(2n)), n>=2. Its profile is -1 when v(x)<=v(z), otherwise -min(1+(v(x)-1)/n,2), and -2 at the point killing x. The tuples consisting of this profile and constant -2 on B are full-fibre-compatible C functions and descend. They increase to the exact raw envelope: -1 on A off the identified point and -2 on B and that point. Valuations (v(x),v(z))=(L,1) approach the point, proving non-USC. Its regularization is -1 there but -2 at B's ordinary valuation, violating the B inequality. It is not D and no maximal D minorant exists. This does not negate the NORMAL residual.

For every excellent reduced curve the link consists of normalization DVR centres, not only irreducible components. Conductor value is finite at every branch, so link fibres are singletons. On a DVR the marked point is an actual effective Cartier divisor and there are no contracted curves. Its negative real multiples give all finite nonpositive slopes, including zero. Full positive G331 descent and the ONE decreasing representation max(u,-j) give every extended branch vector. Thus P_geom(phi)=P_ideal(phi)=min(phi,0), including mixed zero and partial bottom. Gauge factor is ord_q(a)/ord_q(b). B341/E350 reference mass is the actual residue degree times ord_q(a); a branch bottom has positive mass and infinite energy. notes.text:
This is a new residual mechanism, proved from the independently geometric C rather than by defining another psh completion.

Let M_<=1(X) be the weakly compact positive Radon subprobabilities and define J_x={mu:h(x)<=integral h dmu for every h in C}. Delta_x belongs, and J_x is compact convex. Its graph is closed because each defining h is continuous.

The exact dual formula is p(f)(x)=min_(mu in J_x) integral f dmu for every finite continuous f. Competitors give one inequality. For the other, consider the convex cone W={(g,t):some h in C satisfies h<=g and t<=h(x)} in C(X) times R. If t>p(f)(x), then (f,t) is outside its closure: norm convergence (g_i,t_i)->(f,t) would contradict n1's nonexpansivity and t_i<=p(g_i)(x).

Hahn--Banach separation gives L(g,t)=mu(g)-alpha t nonnegative on W and negative at (f,t). The pairs (r,-s), r>=0,s>=0, imply positivity of mu and alpha>=0. If alpha=0, testing the negative constant pairs forces mu(X)=0, contradicting nonzero separation. Divide by alpha>0. The pairs (h,h(x)) give the Jensen inequalities; h=-1 gives mass<=1. Separation gives integral f dmu<t. Let t decrease to p(f)(x); compactness attains the infimum. Hahn--Banach, positive-functional/Radon correspondence and weak compactness are explicitly disclosed ordinary functional foundations; this dual argument itself is new.

CE holds exactly when x->J_x is weakly lower hemicontinuous. Closed graph in a compact ambient measure space already gives upper hemicontinuity and lower semicontinuity of the minimum. Lower hemicontinuity gives its upper semicontinuity, hence CE by the dual formula.

For necessity, suppose lower hemicontinuity fails at x0 for mu0 in J_x0. A weak neighbourhood is specified by finitely many continuous f_j and an Euclidean ball of radius epsilon about their integrals at mu0. There is a net x_i->x0 whose compact convex projected J_xi avoid that ball. Closest-point separation gives unit a_i with a_i dot (projection(mu)-projection(mu0))>=epsilon for all mu in J_xi. A subnet has a_i->a. Uniform boundedness of all projections gives the same inequality for a with epsilon/2 eventually. For f=sum a_j f_j, duality says p(f)(x_i)>=integral f dmu0+epsilon/2, while p(f)(x0)<=integral f dmu0. This contradicts CE. The proof retains nonmetrizable links and actual nets.

A second reduction uses the ACTUAL G331 divisorial inequality g(nu)>=A_nu g(v), with A_nu>0 fixed for all g in C and all v. If continuous f is negative somewhere, divisorial density gives nu with f(nu)<0. Every competitor then has g(v)<=f(nu)/A_nu<0 uniformly over ALL v. Taking the raw supremum preserves the bound without assuming D membership. Thus on a normal branch p(f) is zero exactly when f>=0; otherwise it is uniformly strictly negative. A normal continuous-obstacle counterexample cannot be a mixed-zero spike. It would have to fail upper semicontinuity while bounded and uniformly negative.

This genuinely advances the residual to a geometric measure-continuity question. It does NOT prove lower hemicontinuity for arbitrary excellent normal dimension>=3. Primary correction truncations reverse the required inequality; n6's quadratic family has a good cover; n7's nonnormal obstruction and increasing energy spikes do not supply a normal raw-envelope counterexample. No such normal example was obtained. The original completion criteria are unchanged and original candidate remains false.
